rounds.text: West Leisure Resorts Ltd is trading near the bottom of its yearly range at just 9% of its 52-week span [E5], presenting an attractive entry point given its underlying fundamental momentum [E53]. The company demonstrates accelerating top-line expansion, boasting a 3-year compounded sales growth rate of 24% [E16] alongside signals highlighting massive year-over-year sales surges [E58] and strong sales growth [E59]. This top-line strength is paired with robust bottom-line momentum, as profit growth exceeds 1-year price growth by 267% while profit growth has climbed more than 20% year-over-year [E53, E61]. Furthermore, investors are acquiring these expanding operations at a very modest price-to-book ratio of 1.28x on a book value of ₹ 65.3 per share [E2], aligning closely with a sector benchmark P/B of 1.19x [E7] for a micro-cap valued at ₹ 25.6 Cr [E3]. Conceded: [E1], [E4], [E8], [E17].

West Leisure Resorts Ltd trades at an astronomical P/E ratio of 511x based on filed statements [E1], or alternatively a negative P/E of -216.31x against a sector benchmark of just 20.02x [E6], indicating extreme overvaluation or catastrophic unprofitability that current earnings cannot support. The company generates a negative return on assets (ROA) of -0.55%, severely lagging behind the sector benchmark ROA of 1.8% [E8]. Furthermore, momentum has broken down completely as compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months has contracted by -5% [E17], and the stock sits languishing at a mere 9% of the way up its 52-week range [E5]. This dismal price action is underscored by a negligible dividend yield of 0.12% [E4], offering investors virtually no income return while holding a deeply distressed asset. Conceded: compounded sales growth over 3 years is 24% [E16] and the screen reasons show strong YoY sales and profit growth [E58, E59, E61].

Conceded: the company trades at a high P/E of 511x and a negative P/E of -216.31x [E1, E6], alongside a negative ROA of -0.55% [E8]. However, the bear's focus on short-term earnings multiples ignores the asset backing, as the stock trades at a conservative price-to-book of 1.28x on a book value of ₹ 65.3 [E2], aligning closely with the sector benchmark P/B of 1.35x [E7]. The bear misinterprets the weak 52-week position [E5] and recent TTM sales contraction [E17] by dismissing the underlying growth engine, which boasts a robust 3-year compounded sales growth of 24% [E16] and powerful recent year-over-year sales surges of 191% [E58]. Furthermore, profit growth exceeds 1-year price growth by 267%, signaling that expectations are being outperformed [E53]. This fundamental momentum is reinforced by strong profit growth exceeding 20% YoY [E61], proving that the business is actively translating its strong sales dynamics into operational progress [E59] despite the depressed valuation metrics [E3, E4].
